2026-08-13T03:53:04.2511029Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2511762Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2512111Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2512714Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2513183Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2513720Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2515304Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2517306Z >
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2519649Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2522126Z >
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2522929Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2523721Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2523904Z ### How to Use
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2524144Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2524844Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2525581Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2525764Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2526776Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2527536Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2528158Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2528365Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2528639Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2529181Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2529724Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2530524Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2531380Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2532131Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2532337Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2532961Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2533836Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2534404Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2535098Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2535308Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2535767Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2536638Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2537182Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2538061Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2538767Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2538974Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2539239Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2539667Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2541085Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2542700Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2542873Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2543330Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2544186Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2545017Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2545325Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2545802Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2547019Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2547847Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2548328Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2548535Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2549288Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2550219Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2550394Z ```bash
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2551136Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2552031Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2552762Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2553206Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2553616Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2554438Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2555011Z ```
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2555224Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2555444Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2556423Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2557421Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2558403Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2559426Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2560515Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2561065Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2561252Z ### Notes
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2561472Z 
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2562098Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2563531Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2564798Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2566064Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2567468Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2568592Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2569573Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2570280Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2570691Z <github-context>
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2571313Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-08-13T03:53:04.2666454Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2667371Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2669522Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2670448Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2671340Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2672172Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2673052Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2673946Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2674792Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-08-13T03:53:04.2675699Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
